Sequential recommenders based on Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) (Tang and Wang, 2018), Gated Recurrent Units (GRUs) (Hidasi et al., 2016), and self-attention (Sun et al., 2019; Zhang et al., 2019; Kang and McAuley, 2018; Zhou et al., 2020; Rajput et al., 2023) have become prevalent in the era of deep learning. Notably, leveraging a T5-like backbone, Rajput et al. 2023 formalize recommendation as generative retrieval, i.e., autoregressively decode the identifiers of the target items, and achieve the current SOTA. While structurally resembling LLMs, it lacks their pre-training knowledge and the accompanying natural language reasoning potential. Our proposed approach adopts self-attention for sequential recommendation, specifically harnessing LLMs as backbones. We compare against various baselines from all the classes discussed above.

item.text: {"text":"Candidate-conditioned attention has direct recent precedent: [VISTA (2025 preprint; ICLR 2026)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2510.22049) summarizes user history into multiple cached tokens, then lets each candidate attend to those tokens. This preserves candidate-specific preference extraction while controlling inference cost. Its industrial-scale results support the architecture’s plausibility, but do not establish gains on short Amazon histories. [ReACT (2025)](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S030645732500295X) likewise explores retrieval of relevant historical behaviors, although its LLM-based framework exceeds this task’s no-pretraining constraint.\n\nFor cold items, [SimRec (2024)](https://www.amazon.science/publications/simrec-mitigating-the-cold-start-problem-in-sequential-recommendation-by-integrating-item-similarity) incorporates item similarity through a modified training loss while retaining the architecture and inference cost; it therefore informs a separate loss ablation rather than evidence for candidate attention. Proposed local experiment: retain SASRec sequence states and add candidate-query attention over causally available history, using ID embeddings plus a small title/description token encoder trained from scratch. Compare SASRec, candidate attention with IDs, text-augmented SASRec, and candidate attention with text under identical loss and sampling. Treat improved compatibility matching as a hypothesis: shared words may capture broad association rather than exact compatibility. Measure macro validation HR@10 and full-catalog scoring cost; chunk candidates to bound attention memory."}
